**File layout (plain‑text, Markdown‑friendly)**  
```
/learning‑notes/
  2024‑10‑29.md   ← one file per day (or per sprint)
  2024‑11‑05.md
  …
```

Each entry follows a single‑line convention that can be grepped later:

```
[HH:MM] [SEV] <commit‑hash> – <short description>
NOTE: <what we assumed, what failed, and the corrective insight>
```

**Minimal Bash helper (`log‑note.sh`)**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# Usage: ./log-note.sh high "Missing null‑check in input parser"
SEVERITY=$1
DESC=$2
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%H:%M")
DATE=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d")
FILE="learning-notes/$DATE.md"

# ensure dir exists
mkdir -p learning-notes

# grab current git hash (or “none” if not in a repo)
HASH=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "none")

# append entry
{
  echo "[$TIMESTAMP] [$SEVERITY] $HASH – $DESC"
  echo "NOTE: "
  echo ""
} >> "$FILE"

# stage the file so it lands with the next commit (optional)
git add "$FILE"
```

*How to use* – bind a shortcut in your editor or terminal (`alias ln='~/bin/log-note.sh'`) and type:
```

```
Then fill the `NOTE:` line in the opened file (or edit later). Over time you can extract patterns with:
```bash
grep -h "NOTE:" learning-notes/*.md | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
```
This keeps capture instantaneous while storing the “why” alongside your code history.
